criteria.criterion: After power-cycling the assembled target, the GBM2804H-100T shaft begins rotating without a button press, command, or other manual intervention.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft motion after power-up
preconditions: NUCLEO-G431RB is flashed with the delivered firmware.
X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 is connected to the NUCLEO-G431RB.
GBM2804H-100T is connected to the driver outputs.
The board and motor are powered according to the target-hardware setup.
procedure: Power off the assembled board and motor setup.
Power on the setup.
Observe the motor shaft without sending commands or pressing controls.
criteria.expected: The motor begins the rotation demonstration automatically after power-up.

criteria.criterion: The project build completes and produces the firmware image without build errors.
criteria.observable: Build-tool result and generated firmware image
preconditions: The documented build environment is configured.
The project source and configuration are present.
procedure: Run the documented project build command.
Inspect the build exit status and generated firmware artifact.
criteria.expected: The build exits successfully with no errors and produces a flashable firmware image.

criteria.criterion: The generated firmware image programs the NUCLEO-G431RB successfully and executes after a target reset.
criteria.observable: Programming-tool result and target execution after reset
preconditions: A successful firmware image is available.
A NUCLEO-G431RB is connected to the standard programming interface.
The target hardware is powered.
procedure: Program the generated firmware image onto the NUCLEO-G431RB using the documented standard tool.
Reset or power-cycle the board.
Observe the target's post-reset execution, including the automatic demonstration behavior.
criteria.expected: The programming tool reports successful programming, and the target executes the firmware after reset.

criteria.criterion: The demonstrated firmware execution occurs on a NUCLEO-G431RB board.
criteria.observable: Board identity marking and firmware execution on the connected target
preconditions: A board labeled NUCLEO-G431RB is available.
The delivered firmware is programmed onto that board.
procedure: Verify the board marking identifies it as NUCLEO-G431RB.
Reset or power-cycle the board.
Observe that the programmed firmware executes on that board.
criteria.expected: The board is identified as NUCLEO-G431RB and the firmware runs on it after reset.

criteria.criterion: The hardware assembly and firmware configuration identify the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1/STSPIN830 as the motor driver and use its PWM, GPIO, and EN/FAULT interfaces with settings matching the driver's documented default configuration.
criteria.observable: Assembled-board identification, firmware pin assignments, and driver-initialization configuration
preconditions: The X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 is stacked on the NUCLEO-G431RB.
The STSPIN830 documentation and default configuration are available for comparison.
The firmware source and hardware configuration are available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the assembled driver-board marking.
Inspect the firmware's PWM, GPIO, and EN/FAULT assignments.
Compare the STSPIN830 initialization settings with the documented default configuration.
criteria.expected: The board is an X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1, the firmware uses the STSPIN830 PWM/GPIO/EN/FAULT interfaces, and all inspected settings match the documented defaults.

criteria.criterion: The motor connected to the U/V/W outputs is identified as GBM2804H-100T and its motor specification states seven pole pairs.
criteria.observable: Motor label and motor specification
preconditions: The motor is connected to the driver's U/V/W outputs.
The motor specification or datasheet is available.
procedure: Read the label on the connected motor.
Inspect the applicable motor specification for the pole-pair count.
criteria.expected: The motor label is GBM2804H-100T and the specified pole-pair count is 7 pairs.

criteria.criterion: The DC voltage measured at the motor-driver input during the test is 12 V.
criteria.observable: Voltage-meter reading at the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 driver input
preconditions: The power supply is connected to the driver according to the manufacturer's recommendations.
The assembled setup is powered for the test.
A suitable DC voltage meter is available.
procedure: Power the assembled setup.
Measure the voltage directly at the driver input terminals during the test.
Record the meter reading and polarity.
criteria.expected: The measured input is 12 V DC.

criteria.criterion: The firmware does not attempt to start the motor sequence when the supply is outside the permitted specification.
criteria.rationale: The failure behavior requires an inhibited start, but the requirement does not define the permitted voltage range or provide a named supply-voltage measurement/status interface that can be driven and observed.
criteria.blocked_reason: No allowable supply-voltage range and no observable voltage-validity or motor-start interface are specified, so an out-of-range failure check cannot be made concrete.

criteria.criterion: When TIM1 is enabled, three PWM waveforms are simultaneously observable on the U, V, and W output pins with 120° phase separation between adjacent phases.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces on the U, V, and W pins
preconditions: Board is powered.
TIM1 clock and GPIO clocks are available.
The motor sequence has reached the PWM-enable step.
procedure: Start the firmware and allow the motor sequence to enable PWM.
Probe the U, V, and W output pins with a three-channel oscilloscope.
Measure the phase separation between the three periodic waveforms.
criteria.expected: Three active PWM waveforms are present, with each phase separated from the next by 120° electrical phase.

criteria.criterion: A failed TIM1 initialization leaves the motor-sequence controller in its non-running state and prevents any motor-start command from being issued.
criteria.observable: Motor-sequence state and motor-start command recorded by a fake driver
preconditions: The application flow is tested with the TIM1 initialization callback configured to return failure.
procedure: Inject a TIM1 initialization failure.
Run the startup sequence.
Inspect the motor-sequence state and the fake driver's motor-start command log.
criteria.expected: The sequence remains stopped or aborted, and the motor-start command log is empty.
criteria.rationale: This checks the stated failure behavior using the portable startup/state-machine logic while replacing the hardware initialization with a failing test double.

criteria.criterion: The driver interface configuration selects the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 factory-default three-PWM-input mode and contains no firmware or hardware configuration that selects an alternate input mode.
criteria.observable: Driver-board jumper/settings inspection and firmware GPIO/PWM configuration
preconditions: The assembled driver board uses the factory-default jumper and configuration settings.
procedure: Inspect the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 jumper and mode-selection settings.
Inspect the firmware configuration and initialization code for driver input-mode changes.
Compare the resulting configuration with the STSPIN830 three-PWM-input mode definition.
criteria.expected: The board remains in factory-default three-PWM-input mode, and no alternate-mode selection or reconfiguration is present.

criteria.criterion: During the motor run window, three distinct GPIO signals are present at the STSPIN830 U, V, and W input pins.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces at the three STSPIN830 input pins
preconditions: TIM1 is configured.
The U, V, and W GPIO mappings are configured.
The motor sequence is in its run window.
An oscilloscope is connected to the three driver inputs.
procedure: Start the motor sequence.
Probe the STSPIN830 U, V, and W input pins.
Confirm that each pin has its own PWM waveform during the run window.
criteria.expected: All three U, V, and W inputs show observable PWM activity, and the signals originate from three distinct GPIO outputs.

criteria.criterion: The PWM carrier measured on each of the U, V, and W outputs has a nominal frequency of 20 kHz.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM period or frequency on the U, V, and W output pins
preconditions: TIM1 is configured.
PWM is enabled.
An oscilloscope or frequency counter is connected to each phase output.
procedure: Enable PWM without changing the configured timer clock.
Measure the carrier frequency on U, V, and W.
Record the measured frequency for each output.
criteria.expected: Each phase measures 20 kHz nominally.

criteria.criterion: The PWM-frequency pass/fail band around 20 kHz cannot be asserted until the required measurement tolerance is specified.
criteria.rationale: The stated acceptance criterion requires 20 kHz plus or minus a tolerance, but neither the tolerance value nor a referenced test-plan limit is provided.
criteria.blocked_reason: No numeric PWM frequency tolerance is specified, so a measured value cannot be classified as passing or failing against the requirement.

criteria.criterion: Before the motor-driver EN signal rises, the U, V, and W outputs remain configured but show no PWM switching activity.
criteria.observable: Time-correlated oscilloscope traces for EN, U, V, and W
preconditions: The boot delay has elapsed.
No EN or FAULT condition is active before startup.
The oscilloscope is triggering on the EN rising edge.
procedure: Start the firmware and capture the interval before the EN rising edge at approximately t=3 s.
Inspect the U, V, and W traces before the EN edge.
Verify that GPIO and PWM initialization has completed while the PWM outputs remain disabled.
criteria.expected: Before EN rises, U, V, and W remain at their idle levels with no switching transitions.

criteria.criterion: Immediately after EN rises and PWM is enabled, the first active PWM duty cycle on U, V, and W is 10%.
criteria.observable: First active PWM pulse widths and periods on U, V, and W after the EN rising edge
preconditions: The boot delay has elapsed.
No EN or FAULT condition is active before startup.
The oscilloscope captures EN and all three PWM outputs.
procedure: Trigger an oscilloscope capture on the EN rising edge.
Identify the first active PWM cycle after PWM enable.
Measure the high-time-to-period ratio on U, V, and W.
criteria.expected: The first active duty cycle is 10% on each of U, V, and W.

criteria.criterion: The first active PWM duty cycle is followed by the startup duty-cycle ramp in the defined motor sequence without an EN assertion occurring before PWM/GPIO initialization completes.
criteria.observable: Time-correlated EN, PWM output, and initialization-completion traces or firmware event markers
preconditions: The boot delay has elapsed.
The startup sequence and its duty-cycle timing points are defined.
No EN or FAULT condition is active before startup.
procedure: Capture the startup sequence from before EN assertion through the ramp interval.
Compare the observed duty-cycle changes and event ordering with the defined sequence timing points.
criteria.expected: EN rises only after PWM/GPIO initialization completion, and subsequent duty-cycle changes match every specified startup-sequence timing and value.

criteria.criterion: If the test injects an EN assertion before PWM/GPIO configuration completes, the startup controller deasserts EN, keeps PWM disabled, and aborts the sequence.
criteria.observable: Fake EN output, PWM-enable state, and motor-sequence state
preconditions: The startup controller is tested with a fake EN output and fake PWM/GPIO initialization callbacks.
The EN assertion is injected before the configuration-complete callback.
procedure: Begin the startup sequence.
Inject an early EN assertion before configuration completion.
Allow the safety/error handler to run.
Inspect the fake EN output, PWM-enable state, and sequence state.
criteria.expected: EN is low, PWM remains disabled, and the sequence is in the aborted or stopped state.
criteria.rationale: This directly exercises the specified early-enable failure behavior in the portable startup state machine without requiring an oscilloscope.

criteria.criterion: The complete startup ramp cannot be checked for exact duty-cycle values or timing until the referenced sequence ramp points are specified.
criteria.rationale: The requirement specifies the initial 10% duty cycle but refers to an otherwise undefined ramp sequence; no subsequent duty-cycle values, durations, or slope are provided.
criteria.blocked_reason: The startup ramp lacks explicit duty-cycle and timing values, so exact conformance cannot be asserted beyond the initial 10% check.

criteria.criterion: The oscilloscope capture shall show three sinusoidal-modulated PWM phase waveforms on U, V, and W with 120° phase separation during the run window.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces for PWM outputs U, V, and W
preconditions: Driver enabled
Sequence is in the run window
Oscilloscope probes are connected to U, V, and W
procedure: Start the automatic sequence with the driver enabled.
Capture synchronized U, V, and W waveforms during the run window.
Measure the relative electrical phase of each phase waveform.
criteria.expected: Three sinusoidal-modulated PWM waveforms with 120° separation between adjacent phases.

criteria.criterion: The measured three-phase electrical angle shall progress continuously in one rotating direction during the run window.
criteria.observable: Time-ordered oscilloscope capture of U/V/W phase progression
preconditions: Driver enabled
Sequence is in the run window
procedure: Capture multiple consecutive electrical cycles from U, V, and W.
Compare the phase angle ordering across successive cycles.
criteria.expected: The phase angle advances from cycle to cycle in a consistent rotating direction rather than remaining stationary or reversing.

criteria.criterion: If rotating-field generation fails during the run, all motor PWM outputs shall be disabled and the sequence shall be aborted.
criteria.observable: PWM output levels and sequence state after injected rotating-field failure
preconditions: Driver enabled
A rotating-field generation failure can be injected or detected
procedure: Start the sequence.
Inject or simulate failure of rotating-field generation.
Observe the PWM outputs and sequence state.
criteria.expected: PWM outputs are disabled and the sequence is in an aborted state.
criteria.rationale: Derived from the requirement's explicit failure behavior; the observable consequences are PWM disablement and sequence abortion.

criteria.criterion: PWM duty shall increase monotonically from the initial amplitude to the maximum amplitude during the startup ramp, with no consecutive control-update change greater than 5 percentage points.
criteria.observable: Timestamped PWM duty measurements at each control update from t=3 s through t=8 s
preconditions: Driver enabled at t=3 s
Startup ramp window is active
PWM duty can be measured at consecutive control updates
procedure: Start the sequence and record PWM duty at every control update from t=3 s to t=8 s.
Compare each duty value with the preceding value.
Check the largest consecutive change.
criteria.expected: Each duty value is greater than or equal to the preceding value, and every consecutive increase is ≤5 percentage points.

criteria.criterion: PWM amplitude shall reach 20% by the end of the startup ramp at t=8 s.
criteria.observable: PWM duty measurement at t=8 s
preconditions: Driver enabled at t=3 s
Startup ramp window is active
procedure: Run the sequence from t=3 s through t=8 s.
Measure PWM duty at t=8 s.
criteria.expected: PWM duty is 20% at or before t=8 s.

criteria.criterion: If the PWM amplitude ramp cannot be achieved, PWM shall be disabled and the driver shall enter standby.
criteria.observable: PWM output state and driver state after injected ramp failure
preconditions: Driver enabled
Startup amplitude ramp is active
A ramp failure can be injected or detected
procedure: Start the startup amplitude ramp.
Inject or simulate an inability to achieve the requested ramp.
Observe PWM outputs and the driver state.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled and the driver is in standby.
criteria.rationale: Derived from the requirement's explicit failure behavior.

criteria.criterion: Measured electrical frequency shall increase monotonically from 1 Hz at t=3 s to 10 Hz by t=8 s.
criteria.observable: Timestamped electrical-frequency measurements from t=3 s through t=8 s
preconditions: Boot delay elapsed
Driver enabled at t=3 s
No active EN or FAULT condition
procedure: Start frequency measurement at t=3 s.
Record frequency through t=8 s.
Check the initial value, final value, and ordering of all samples.
criteria.expected: Frequency is 1 Hz at t=3 s, is nondecreasing at all sampled times, and reaches 10 Hz no later than t=8 s.

criteria.criterion: If the electrical-frequency ramp cannot be achieved, PWM shall be disabled and the driver shall enter standby.
criteria.observable: PWM output state and driver state after injected frequency-ramp failure
preconditions: Frequency startup ramp is active
A frequency-ramp failure can be injected or detected
procedure: Start the frequency ramp.
Inject or simulate inability to achieve the requested frequency ramp.
Observe PWM outputs and the driver state.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled and the driver is in standby.
criteria.rationale: Derived from the requirement's explicit failure behavior.

criteria.criterion: Measured PWM duty shall increase monotonically from 10% at t=3 s to 20% by t=8 s.
criteria.observable: Timestamped PWM duty measurements from t=3 s through t=8 s
preconditions: Boot delay elapsed
Driver enabled at t=3 s
procedure: Measure PWM duty at t=3 s and at successive points through t=8 s.
Check monotonic ordering and endpoint values.
criteria.expected: Duty is 10% at t=3 s, never decreases during the interval, and reaches 20% no later than t=8 s.

criteria.criterion: If the PWM amplitude ramp cannot be achieved, PWM shall be disabled and the driver shall enter standby.
criteria.observable: PWM output state and driver state after injected amplitude-ramp failure
preconditions: Amplitude startup ramp is active
An amplitude-ramp failure can be injected or detected
procedure: Start the amplitude ramp.
Inject or simulate inability to achieve the requested amplitude ramp.
Observe PWM outputs and the driver state.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled and the driver is in standby.
criteria.rationale: Derived from the requirement's explicit failure behavior.

criteria.criterion: Measured electrical frequency shall remain nominally 10 Hz for the entire hold window from t=8 s through t=18 s.
criteria.observable: Electrical-frequency measurements throughout t=8–18 s
preconditions: Startup ramp completed
Electrical frequency has reached 10 Hz
procedure: Measure electrical frequency repeatedly from t=8 s through t=18 s.
Compare each measurement with the 10 Hz setpoint.
criteria.expected: 10 Hz throughout the hold window; the allowable measurement tolerance must be supplied by the requirements or test configuration.

criteria.criterion: If the held electrical frequency deviates from its required value, the sequence shall enter the shutdown ramp at t=18 s.
criteria.observable: Sequence state and frequency-ramp command at t=18 s after an induced deviation
preconditions: Hold window is active
A frequency deviation can be induced or detected
procedure: Induce or simulate a frequency deviation during t=8–18 s.
Allow the sequence to reach t=18 s.
Observe the sequence state and commanded frequency.
criteria.expected: The shutdown-ramp state is entered at t=18 s.

criteria.criterion: Measured PWM duty shall not exceed 20% at any sampled time from t=8 s through t=18 s.
criteria.observable: Timestamped PWM duty measurements throughout the hold window
preconditions: Startup ramp completed
Hold window is active
procedure: Measure PWM duty continuously or at a sampling rate sufficient to capture control updates from t=8 s through t=18 s.
Find the maximum measured duty.
criteria.expected: Maximum PWM duty is ≤20%.

criteria.criterion: If PWM duty exceeds 20% during the hold window, the firmware shall immediately start the shutdown ramp.
criteria.observable: Shutdown-ramp transition following an induced over-amplitude condition
preconditions: Hold window is active
An over-amplitude condition can be induced or detected
procedure: Induce or simulate PWM duty above 20%.
Observe the next control-state transition.
criteria.expected: The shutdown ramp starts immediately after the over-amplitude condition is detected.

criteria.criterion: Electrical frequency shall be 1 Hz at t=3 s and shall reach 10 Hz by t=8 s while increasing monotonically during the startup ramp.
criteria.observable: Timestamped electrical-frequency measurements during t=3–8 s
preconditions: Startup ramp window is active
procedure: Record electrical frequency at t=3 s and at each control update through t=8 s.
Check endpoint values and monotonic ordering.
criteria.expected: Frequency is 1 Hz at t=3 s, every subsequent value is ≥ the preceding value, and frequency reaches 10 Hz no later than t=8 s.

criteria.criterion: The electrical-frequency increase between consecutive control updates shall never exceed 1 Hz during t=3–8 s.
criteria.observable: Electrical-frequency value associated with each consecutive control update
preconditions: Startup ramp window is active
Control-update timing and frequency values are observable
procedure: Record the frequency at every consecutive control update during t=3–8 s.
Subtract each previous value from the next value.
criteria.expected: Every positive step is ≤1 Hz; no negative step occurs.

criteria.criterion: If the frequency ramp cannot be achieved, PWM shall be disabled and the driver shall return to standby.
criteria.observable: PWM output state and driver state after injected frequency-ramp failure
preconditions: Startup frequency ramp is active
A ramp failure can be injected or detected
procedure: Start the startup frequency ramp.
Inject or simulate inability to meet the ramp criteria.
Observe PWM outputs and the driver state.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled and the driver is in standby.
criteria.rationale: Derived from the requirement's explicit failure behavior.

criteria.criterion: PWM duty measured at the beginning of the startup ramp shall be 10% at t=3 s.
criteria.observable: PWM duty at t=3 s
preconditions: Driver enabled at t=3 s
PWM enabled
Startup ramp begins at t=3 s
procedure: Trigger the measurement from the boot-time reference.
Measure PWM duty at t=3 s when the startup ramp begins.
criteria.expected: PWM duty is 10%.

criteria.criterion: The maximum measured PWM duty shall be no greater than 20% at every observation time during the automatic sequence.
criteria.observable: Maximum timestamped PWM duty from sequence start through shutdown
preconditions: Sequence is running
PWM duty is measured at all control updates or continuously
procedure: Run the complete automatic sequence.
Record PWM duty throughout the sequence, including startup, hold, and shutdown.
Determine the maximum recorded duty.
criteria.expected: Maximum PWM duty is ≤20%.

criteria.criterion: If PWM duty exceeds 20%, the firmware shall start the shutdown response and disable outputs at t=20 s.
criteria.observable: Shutdown-ramp transition and PWM output state at t=20 s after an induced over-limit condition
preconditions: Sequence is running
An over-limit PWM condition can be induced or detected
procedure: Induce or simulate PWM duty above 20%.
Observe the transition into shutdown.
Check PWM outputs at t=20 s.
criteria.expected: Shutdown begins after the violation and PWM outputs are disabled at t=20 s.

criteria.criterion: The GBM2804H-100T shall exhibit visible movement or rotation continuously or intermittently during the automatic run window from t=3 s through t=20 s.
criteria.observable: Direct visual observation or video recording of the motor shaft/rotor
preconditions: Sequence started successfully
Driver enabled
Motor and mechanical load are installed
procedure: Start the automatic sequence.
Observe or record the motor from t=3 s through t=20 s.
Determine whether visible shaft or rotor motion occurs during the interval.
criteria.expected: Visible motor movement or rotation is observed at least once during t=3–20 s.

criteria.criterion: Motor motion shall cease at or after t=20 s.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft/rotor motion and PWM output state after t=20 s
preconditions: Automatic sequence has completed its run window
Motor is mechanically observable
procedure: Run the sequence through t=20 s.
Observe the motor after t=20 s and verify the output state.
criteria.expected: No visible motor movement remains after t=20 s, and motor-driving PWM is disabled.

criteria.criterion: With no UART activity, the first sequence-start output occurs at 3.0 s after boot, within one scheduler tick.
criteria.observable: PWM activity and driver EN transition measured from reset release
preconditions: PWM and GPIO are initialized.
EN and FAULT are inactive.
The board has been reset or power-cycled.
No UART bytes are transmitted.
procedure: Reset or power-cycle the board and start a timer at reset release.
Monitor driver EN and PWM outputs without transmitting UART data.
Record the timestamp of the first driver-enable or startup-ramp event.
criteria.expected: The first sequence-start event occurs at 3.0 s ± one scheduler tick; no UART input is required.

criteria.criterion: Motor motion is sustained throughout the 10 s hold interval after startup completes, and shutdown begins when that interval ends.
criteria.observable: Motor motion and PWM frequency/amplitude during the hold interval
preconditions: The automatic sequence has started successfully.
The startup ramp has completed at approximately t=8 s.
The driver and motor are connected.
procedure: Reset the board and monitor the motor and PWM output from boot.
Verify startup completes at approximately t=8 s.
Observe the motor and PWM output through t=18 s.
criteria.expected: Motion remains present throughout t=8 s through t=18 s, and the shutdown ramp begins at approximately t=18 s.

criteria.criterion: Driver EN transitions to its enabled level at approximately 3 s after boot and remains enabled until shutdown.
criteria.observable: Motor-driver EN GPIO level versus boot-relative time
preconditions: The board has been reset or power-cycled.
Boot delay has not been bypassed.
No EN or FAULT condition is asserted.
procedure: Reset the board and start a boot-relative timer.
Probe the driver EN pin throughout the sequence.
Record the enable transition and the subsequent transition to standby.
criteria.expected: EN becomes enabled at 3.0 s ± one scheduler tick and remains enabled until the shutdown sequence completes.

criteria.criterion: Electrical frequency decreases monotonically during the shutdown ramp.
criteria.observable: Measured electrical frequency from t=18 s to t=20 s
preconditions: The automatic sequence has reached the end of the hold window.
Frequency measurement equipment is connected to the motor or drive output.
procedure: Reset the board and measure electrical frequency continuously from boot.
Capture frequency samples during t=18 s through t=20 s.
Compare each successive sample with the preceding sample.
criteria.expected: Frequency never increases during t=18 s to t=20 s.

criteria.criterion: Electrical frequency reaches 0 Hz no later than 20 s after boot.
criteria.observable: Measured electrical frequency at t=20 s and thereafter
preconditions: The hold window has completed.
Frequency measurement equipment is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure electrical frequency from boot.
Check the frequency at t=20 s and after the shutdown ramp.
criteria.expected: Measured electrical frequency is 0 Hz by t=20 s and remains 0 Hz after the ramp.

criteria.criterion: PWM duty decreases monotonically during the shutdown ramp.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM duty cycle from t=18 s to t=20 s
preconditions: The automatic sequence has reached the end of the hold window.
A PWM measurement instrument is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure PWM duty cycle from boot.
Capture duty-cycle samples during t=18 s through t=20 s.
Compare each successive sample with the preceding sample.
criteria.expected: PWM duty never increases during t=18 s to t=20 s.

criteria.criterion: PWM duty reaches 0% no later than 20 s after boot.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM duty cycle at t=20 s and thereafter
preconditions: The hold window has completed.
A PWM measurement instrument is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure PWM duty cycle from boot.
Check the duty cycle at t=20 s and after the shutdown ramp.
criteria.expected: Measured PWM duty is 0% by t=20 s and remains 0% afterward.

criteria.criterion: No PWM switching activity is present at or after 20 s from boot.
criteria.observable: PWM output waveform after t=20 s
preconditions: The shutdown ramp has completed.
A sufficiently long-bandwidth oscilloscope or logic analyzer is connected to the PWM output.
procedure: Reset the board and monitor the PWM output from boot.
Inspect the output at t=20 s and for the remainder of the post-run observation period.
criteria.expected: The PWM output has no rising or falling switching edges at any time t≥20 s.

criteria.criterion: Driver EN is deasserted at or after 20 s from boot.
criteria.observable: Motor-driver EN GPIO level after t=20 s
preconditions: The shutdown ramp has completed.
The EN pin is accessible to a logic analyzer or oscilloscope.
procedure: Reset the board and monitor EN from boot.
Check EN at t=20 s and throughout the post-run observation period.
criteria.expected: EN is deasserted no later than t=20 s and remains deasserted.

criteria.criterion: After the automatic sequence completes, no PWM switching or motor motion occurs before a subsequent reset or power cycle.
criteria.observable: PWM waveform and motor motion after sequence completion
preconditions: The automatic sequence has completed at t≥20 s.
The board is not reset or power-cycled during the observation interval.
The motor and PWM output are observable.
procedure: Allow the board to complete the automatic sequence.
Continue monitoring PWM and motor motion without sending a reset or power-cycle command.
Reset or power-cycle the board only after the post-run observation.
criteria.expected: No PWM edges and no motor motion occur for the entire observation interval after t=20 s and before the subsequent reset or power cycle.

criteria.criterion: The elapsed time from reset release to sequence start is 3.0 s within one scheduler tick.
criteria.observable: Boot-relative timestamp of the first startup-ramp or driver-enable event
preconditions: The board has been reset or power-cycled.
The driver is initially disabled.
No UART input is provided.
procedure: Reset or power-cycle the board and start a timer at reset release.
Monitor the driver EN and PWM outputs.
Record the timestamp of the first sequence-start event.
criteria.expected: Sequence start occurs at 3.0 s ± one scheduler tick after reset release.

criteria.criterion: The startup frequency and amplitude ramps both complete within the interval from t=3 s through t=8 s.
criteria.observable: Measured frequency and PWM amplitude at the startup-ramp endpoint
preconditions: The boot delay has elapsed.
Frequency and PWM measurement equipment is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure frequency and PWM amplitude from boot.
Identify the start of the ramp at approximately t=3 s.
Verify that both ramp outputs have reached their hold-state values by t=8 s.
criteria.expected: Both startup ramps are complete no later than t=8.0 s, giving a duration of no more than 5.0 s from t=3 s.

criteria.criterion: The sequence remains in the hold state from t=8 s through t=18 s.
criteria.observable: Measured electrical frequency and PWM duty during the hold interval
preconditions: The startup ramp has completed.
Frequency and PWM measurement equipment is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure frequency and PWM duty from boot.
Check the values continuously or at a sampling rate sufficient to detect departure from the hold state during t=8 s through t=18 s.
Record the transition into the shutdown ramp.
criteria.expected: The hold state lasts 10.0 s from t=8 s to t=18 s, with electrical frequency at 10 Hz and PWM duty no greater than 20%; shutdown begins at t=18 s.

criteria.criterion: The shutdown ramp lasts 2.0 s from t=18 s to t=20 s and reaches zero frequency and zero PWM amplitude by its end.
criteria.observable: Measured frequency and PWM duty throughout the shutdown ramp
preconditions: The hold window has completed at approximately t=18 s.
Frequency and PWM measurement equipment is connected.
procedure: Reset the board and measure frequency and PWM duty from boot.
Capture the start of the shutdown ramp at t=18 s.
Verify both values reach zero by t=20 s.
criteria.expected: The shutdown ramp starts at t=18.0 s, ends at t=20.0 s, and both electrical frequency and PWM duty are zero at or before t=20.0 s.

criteria.criterion: When EN/FAULT is asserted during any sequence phase, all PWM outputs stop within one control cycle and no later than 10 ms.
criteria.observable: U, V, and W PWM output waveforms and the EN/FAULT input edge timestamp
preconditions: The automatic sequence is active at a known phase.
The motor-driver PWM outputs are connected to an oscilloscope or logic analyzer.
EN/FAULT is inactive before the test.
procedure: Start the automatic sequence and wait until PWM is active.
Assert EN/FAULT while the sequence is running.
Measure the time from the EN/FAULT assertion edge to the last PWM transition on each of U, V, and W.
criteria.expected: Each PWM output has no transitions after the fault response point, and the response occurs within one control cycle and less than 10 ms after EN/FAULT assertion.

criteria.criterion: After EN/FAULT is asserted, clearing the fault without applying the required reset or power-cycle does not produce any PWM output.
criteria.observable: U, V, and W PWM output waveforms after EN/FAULT is cleared
preconditions: A sequence is running and PWM is active.
EN/FAULT has been asserted and PWM has stopped.
The required reset or power-cycle has not been applied.
procedure: Assert EN/FAULT and confirm that PWM stops.
Clear EN/FAULT while leaving the MCU powered and not resetting it.
Observe all PWM outputs for the remainder of the test interval.
criteria.expected: No PWM transitions occur after EN/FAULT is cleared until the specified reset or power-cycle sequence is performed.
criteria.rationale: The postconditions state that PWM remains disabled until the fault clears and reset/power-cycle rules are satisfied; this checks the safety-relevant persistence of the disabled state without inventing a recovery mechanism.

criteria.criterion: A deliberate control-task hang during the 8–18 s hold window causes a hardware-watchdog reset.
criteria.observable: MCU reset-cause register or boot diagnostic identifying the watchdog reset
preconditions: The automatic sequence has entered the 8–18 s hold window.
The hardware watchdog is configured and running.
A test hook can deliberately stop the control task.
procedure: Start the automatic sequence and enter the hold window.
Trigger the deliberate control-task hang.
Wait for the MCU to restart.
Read the reset-cause register or capture the boot diagnostic.
criteria.expected: The MCU restarts and the recorded reset cause identifies a hardware-watchdog reset.

criteria.criterion: After a watchdog-induced reset, PWM remains inactive and the motor driver remains in standby throughout the first 3 seconds of boot.
criteria.observable: U, V, and W PWM waveforms plus the driver EN/standby signal from the watchdog reset timestamp
preconditions: The control task is hung during the automatic sequence.
A hardware watchdog reset has occurred.
PWM outputs and the driver EN/standby signal are connected to measurement equipment.
procedure: Trigger the deliberate control-task hang during the hold window.
Record the watchdog reset timestamp.
Observe PWM outputs and driver EN/standby from reset through 3 seconds after reset.
criteria.expected: No PWM switching is observed and driver EN remains deasserted/standby asserted continuously from reset through t=3.000 s.

criteria.criterion: After an active EN/FAULT condition stops the run, clearing EN/FAULT without reset or power-cycle does not re-enable the driver or generate PWM for at least the demo duration.
criteria.observable: Driver EN/standby signal and U, V, and W PWM output waveforms after fault clearance
preconditions: The automatic sequence is running and PWM is active.
The EN/FAULT input is connected and can be asserted and cleared.
The system remains powered without reset or power-cycle.
procedure: Assert EN/FAULT during the run and confirm PWM stops.
Clear EN/FAULT without resetting or power-cycling the MCU.
Observe the driver EN/standby signal and all PWM outputs for at least the full demo duration.
criteria.expected: For the entire observation interval, driver EN remains deasserted/standby remains asserted and no PWM transitions occur.

criteria.criterion: Following each supported reset source, no PWM switching occurs and the driver EN signal remains deasserted for the first 3 seconds after reset.
criteria.observable: U, V, and W PWM waveforms and driver EN/standby signal from each reset timestamp
preconditions: The board can be subjected individually to power-on, external reset, watchdog timeout, and brown-out reset.
PWM outputs and driver EN/standby are connected to measurement equipment.
EN/FAULT is inactive unless the reset test specifically requires otherwise.
procedure: Apply one reset source and record the reset timestamp.
Observe U, V, and W and driver EN/standby continuously through t=3.000 s.
Repeat for power-on, external reset, watchdog timeout, and brown-out.
criteria.expected: For every reset source, no PWM transition is observed before t=3.000 s and driver EN remains deasserted/standby asserted throughout that interval.

criteria.criterion: After the 3-second boot delay, the sequence does not perform an enable action while EN/FAULT is active.
criteria.observable: Driver EN signal and PWM output waveforms after t=3 s with EN/FAULT asserted
preconditions: The board has completed a reset and the 3-second boot interval.
EN/FAULT is active at or after the end of the boot delay.
PWM outputs and driver EN/standby are connected to measurement equipment.
procedure: Reset the MCU with EN/FAULT active.
Maintain EN/FAULT active through and beyond t=3 s.
Observe driver EN and U, V, and W PWM outputs after the boot delay.
criteria.expected: Driver EN remains deasserted/standby remains asserted and no PWM switching starts while EN/FAULT is active.
criteria.rationale: The stated acceptance criteria permit enabling after 3 seconds only if no EN/FAULT is active; this check covers the explicit safety condition that prevents the post-delay sequence from enabling during an active fault.

criteria.criterion: The design and test artifacts contain only MCU I/O, STSPIN830 U/V/W drive, PWM/GPIO, and motor-connectivity verification for the basic rotation demo.
criteria.observable: Design documents, test artifacts, source tree, and configuration
preconditions: The release source tree and associated design/test artifacts are available for review.
procedure: Review the stated project scope and test plan.
Search the source tree and configuration for implemented control features beyond MCU I/O, STSPIN830 drive, PWM/GPIO, and motor connectivity.
Confirm that no additional control feature is included.
criteria.expected: All documented and implemented scope is limited to MCU I/O, STSPIN830 U/V/W driving, PWM/GPIO, motor connections, and the basic rotation demo.

criteria.criterion: The firmware source contains no sensorless FOC algorithm or transform and its PWM generation is open-loop sinusoidal.
criteria.observable: Firmware source and PWM-generation implementation
preconditions: The complete firmware source tree is available for review.
procedure: Search the source and configuration for FOC algorithms, feedback-dependent PWM control, and FOC-related transforms.
Inspect the PWM-generation path to determine whether its waveform is generated without sensor feedback.
Confirm that the implementation is open-loop sinusoidal PWM.
criteria.expected: No FOC algorithm or transform is present, and PWM is generated as open-loop sinusoidal PWM.

criteria.criterion: The firmware source contains no rotor-observer or rotor-estimator module, call, or configuration entry.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree and build configuration
preconditions: The complete firmware source tree and build configuration are available.
procedure: Search for rotor observer, estimator, position-estimation, and equivalent modules or calls.
Inspect the build configuration for any enabled observer or estimator component.
criteria.expected: No rotor-observer or rotor-estimator module, call, or enabled configuration entry is present.

criteria.criterion: The firmware source contains no Clarke or Park transform implementation or call.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree
preconditions: The complete firmware source tree is available.
procedure: Search for Clarke/Park transform names and equivalent αβ or dq coordinate calculations.
Inspect motor-control and PWM code for αβ or dq transform operations.
criteria.expected: No code performing Clarke or Park transforms, including αβ or dq transformations, is present.

criteria.criterion: The firmware source and configuration contain no phase-current PI controller or speed PI controller.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree and control configuration
preconditions: The complete firmware source and configuration are available.
procedure: Search for PI/PID controller implementations and instances.
Inspect control configuration for phase-current or speed controller gains and enable flags.
criteria.expected: No PI controller for phase current or speed exists in source or configuration.

criteria.criterion: No ADC channel, conversion result, or ADC-processing path is used to control phase-current PWM or motor operation.
criteria.observable: ADC configuration and firmware control paths
preconditions: The complete ADC configuration and firmware source are available.
procedure: Inspect ADC channel configuration and conversion-processing code.
Trace every ADC result used by motor-control code.
Confirm that no result represents or controls phase current.
criteria.expected: ADC is not used to sense phase currents for control purposes.

criteria.criterion: No ADC channel, conversion result, or ADC-processing path is used to control the motor from measured DC-bus voltage.
criteria.observable: ADC configuration and firmware control paths
preconditions: The complete ADC configuration and firmware source are available.
procedure: Inspect ADC channel configuration and conversion-processing code.
Trace ADC values into PWM, frequency, enable, or protection decisions.
Confirm that no ADC result represents or controls VBUS.
criteria.expected: ADC is not used to sense DC-bus voltage for control purposes.

criteria.criterion: The project configuration and firmware contain no ADC-triggered DMA enablement or request path.
criteria.observable: ADC, DMA, and trigger configuration plus initialization code
preconditions: The complete project configuration and initialization source are available.
procedure: Inspect ADC configuration for DMA requests or DMA-trigger settings.
Inspect DMA channel configuration and initialization for ADC sources or ADC-triggered transfers.
Confirm that no ADC-triggered DMA path is enabled.
criteria.expected: No ADC-triggered DMA configuration or code path is present.

criteria.criterion: The firmware contains no routine that measures, computes, stores, or applies phase-current offsets.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree and persistent/configuration storage definitions
preconditions: The complete firmware source and configuration are available.
procedure: Search for current-offset calibration routines, offset variables, calibration commands, and stored calibration data.
Inspect initialization and motor-start paths for phase-current offset measurement or application.
criteria.expected: No phase-current offset measurement, storage, or application routine exists.

criteria.criterion: The firmware source and project configuration contain no oscilloscope capture, streaming, or scope-integration code.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree and project configuration
preconditions: The complete firmware source and project configuration are available.
procedure: Search for oscilloscope, scope capture, waveform streaming, trigger, and probe-interface code.
Inspect enabled middleware and configuration for scope integration.
criteria.expected: No oscilloscope integration, capture path, or streaming implementation is present.

criteria.criterion: The firmware contains no speed sensor or estimator input and reports or logs no RPM value.
criteria.observable: Firmware source, configuration, logging strings, and telemetry definitions
preconditions: The complete firmware source and configuration are available.
procedure: Search for speed sensors, rotor-speed estimators, RPM variables, RPM conversion code, and speed logging/reporting.
Inspect the motor test sequence for any speed measurement or output.
criteria.expected: No speed sensor or estimator is used, and no RPM value is reported or logged.

criteria.criterion: The firmware contains no UART command handler that starts, stops, or otherwise controls the automatic motor sequence.
criteria.observable: UART receive handlers, command tables, and sequence-control call sites
preconditions: The complete firmware source and UART configuration are available.
procedure: Inspect UART receive and command-dispatch code.
Trace all UART-controlled calls into motor enable, disable, sequence start, stop, or state transitions.
criteria.expected: No UART input path can start, stop, or otherwise control the automatic sequence.

criteria.criterion: With UART disconnected or receiving arbitrary commands, the automatic sequence starts after the boot delay and completes according to its timeline without UART-dependent state changes.
criteria.observable: Motor-sequence state, PWM enable/output, and driver EN/FAULT behavior on the NUCLEO-G431RB setup
preconditions: The NUCLEO-G431RB, STSPIN830 board, motor, and required power connections are installed.
PWM/GPIO initialization succeeds and no STSPIN830 fault is active.
The UART is either disconnected or connected to a source capable of sending arbitrary bytes.
procedure: Reset the board with UART disconnected and observe the sequence through its complete timeline.
Repeat the reset while sending arbitrary UART bytes throughout the boot delay and sequence.
Compare the start time, stop time, and sequence states between the disconnected and arbitrary-input runs.
criteria.expected: Both runs start after the defined boot delay and complete the same timeline; UART input causes no start, stop, or other sequence-state transition.

criteria.criterion: The firmware and test artifacts contain no speed feedback loop, RPM target, or electrical-frequency adjustment based on measured speed.
criteria.observable: Firmware source, test code, and control configuration
preconditions: The complete firmware, test source, and configuration are available.
procedure: Search for speed feedback inputs, RPM targets, speed-error calculations, and speed-controller gains.
Trace electrical-frequency updates and confirm they do not depend on measured speed.
Inspect test artifacts for speed-regulation or RPM-control procedures.
criteria.expected: No closed-loop speed-regulation path, RPM target, or speed-dependent electrical-frequency adjustment is present or enabled.

criteria.criterion: The firmware contains no automatic or manual code path that estimates, identifies, characterizes, or stores motor resistance, inductance, or flux parameters.
criteria.observable: Firmware source tree, command paths, persistent storage definitions, and test artifacts
preconditions: The complete firmware, configuration, and motor-test artifacts are available.
procedure: Search for resistance, inductance, flux, parameter-identification, characterization, injection, measurement, and storage routines.
Inspect manual command paths and automatic startup/sequence paths for motor-parameter estimation.
Inspect persistent storage definitions for identified motor parameters.
criteria.expected: No code path or routine estimates, identifies, characterizes, or stores motor electrical parameters R, L, or flux.

criteria.criterion: After reset, the automatic sequence enters its running state only when PWM/GPIO initialization has succeeded, the 3 s boot delay has elapsed, and EN/FAULT indicates no active STSPIN830 fault.
criteria.observable: Automatic-sequence state and PWM/driver-enable state on the MCU
preconditions: The MCU is reset or powered on.
The STSPIN830 and motor connections are available.
The test can control or inject PWM/GPIO initialization status and EN/FAULT status.
procedure: Reset the MCU with PWM/GPIO initialization successful and EN/FAULT inactive.
Measure the sequence state before 3 s and at or after 3 s.
Repeat with each dependency made false in turn: failed initialization, boot delay not elapsed, and active EN/FAULT.
Record the sequence state and PWM/driver-enable outputs for each case.
criteria.expected: The sequence remains stopped before 3 s and starts after 3 s only in the all-true case; it does not start in any case where one dependency is false.

criteria.criterion: When any automatic-sequence dependency is false, PWM remains disabled and the STSPIN830 remains in standby.
criteria.observable: PWM output pins and STSPIN830 enable/standby signal
preconditions: The NUCLEO-G431RB and STSPIN830 are connected.
At least one of PWM/GPIO initialization, boot-delay completion, or EN/FAULT-clear status is intentionally false.
procedure: Apply each dependency-failure condition separately.
Observe the PWM output pins and the STSPIN830 enable/standby signal.
Confirm that no motor-driving PWM is emitted while the dependency is false.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled and the driver is in standby for every dependency-failure condition.

criteria.criterion: With ADC measurements, motor-parameter characterization, FOC, observer, current sensing, UART commands, and closed-loop control disabled or absent, the automatic sequence starts and completes according to the defined timeline.
criteria.observable: Automatic-sequence state transitions and PWM enable/output on the MCU
preconditions: PWM/GPIO initialization has succeeded.
The 3 s boot delay has elapsed.
EN/FAULT indicates no active STSPIN830 fault.
All listed optional features are disabled or absent.
procedure: Build and run the firmware with ADC control paths, characterization, FOC, observer, current sensing, UART command handling, and closed-loop control disabled or absent.
Reset the MCU and wait for the boot delay.
Observe the sequence state and PWM output through the entire defined automatic-sequence timeline.
criteria.expected: The sequence starts after the boot delay and reaches each defined timeline state through completion without requiring any listed feature.
